executive_summary: 3-hour memory validation of 12x Samsung 96 GB DDR5-6400 Registered ECC DIMMs (1.15 TB total) in server 172.16.13.217 (Tyrone MDA200A2N-224, dual AMD EPYC 9135). Two back-to-back phases: a 2-hour stress-ng --vm-method all --verify pattern sweep across an 832 GB rolling working set, and a 30-minute memtester burn that locked 1088 GB (96.0% of RAM) into physical memory.

All 12 DIMMs were detected by BMC, BIOS and kernel, EDAC remained clean throughout, and zero memtester failures were recorded - zero ECC errors across all 24 ranks and zero machine-check events in the 2h33m window.

Aggregate STREAM bandwidth of 443 GB/s and NUMA behaviour are at the top of the EPYC 9135 / DDR5-6000 envelope for this 12-of-24 channel layout. The modules are healthy and the server is fit for production memory-bound workloads.

comparison.caption: Channel scaling on the same EPYC 9135 server: prior 4-of-12 layout vs this 12-of-24 layout.
comparison.notes: Aggregate STREAM scales 1.81x from a 1.5x channel-count increase (extra ~20% from better interleave). Filling all 24 channels would push aggregate toward ~580 GB/s. Both layouts run at the EPYC 1DPC-clamped 6000 MT/s.

dmesg_status: 0 machine-check events in the 2h33m window. amd64_edac enumerated 24 ranks (2 ranks x 12 DIMMs); all CE=0 / UE=0 on mc0 + mc1, baseline and post-test.
findings: All 12 Samsung 96 GB DDR5-6400 modules are electrically and structurally healthy: 2 hours of write-and-verify across 52 stress-ng patterns plus 30 minutes at 96.0% RAM residency (1.09 TB pinned) produced zero ECC errors at controller, rank and DIMM level.
BIOS identifies every module's SPD correctly (96 GB / DDR5-6400 rated / Samsung); configured at 6000 MT/s by the EPYC Turin 1DPC platform clamp. ECC active; amd64_edac enumerates 24 ranks, all clean.
Kernel logged 0 machine-check events during the 2h33m window; BMC SEL added 0 new entries. mlock() succeeded on all 64 memtester workers (96% of RAM pinned without reclaim/OOM/swap).
Bandwidth scales linearly with channel population: 12-of-24 yields 443 GB/s, 1.81x the earlier 4-of-12 configuration, near the upper bound of the 1DPC DDR5-6000 envelope.
recommendations: Modules cleared for production: no DIMM action required; the 1.15 TB configuration is qualified for memory-bound workloads (in-memory DBs, large caches, AI inference, virtualization).
Optional 8-hour soak with the same Phase 2 config to convert from infant-mortality clean to burn-in qualified before shipping.
Populate the remaining 12 channels (full 24-of-24) to push aggregate STREAM from 443 GB/s toward ~580 GB/s - pure bandwidth headroom.
Enable BIOS patrol scrub (RAS) to catch single-bit errors during idle, and install rasdaemon for continuous per-DIMM error history.
